'''Lurdes Yoshiko Tani Inoue''' is a Brazilian-born statistician of Japanese descent, who specializes in [[Bayesian inference]]. She works as a professor of [[biostatistics]] in the [[University of Washington School of Public Health]].<ref name="closeup">[http://sph.washington.edu/news/closeup/profile.asp?content_ID=1613 Close up August 2012: Lurdes Inoue], [[University of Washington School of Public Health]], retrieved 2016-07-13.</ref>

==Education and career==
Inoue's grandparents emigrated from Japan to Brazil in the 1930s; she was born in [[São Paulo]], where she grew up.<ref name="closeup"/>

She earned bachelor's and master's degree from the [[University of São Paulo]] in 1992 and 1995,<ref name="profile">[http://sph.washington.edu/faculty/fac_bio.asp?url_ID=Inoue_lurdes Faculty profile], [[University of Washington School of Public Health]], retrieved 2016-07-13.</ref> and received a fellowship from the Brazilian government to continue her studies in the US.<ref name="closeup"/> She completed her Ph.D. in [[statistics]] in 1999 from [[Duke University]],<ref name="profile"/> under the supervision of [[Don Berry (statistician)|Don Berry]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=47992}}</ref>

After postdoctoral research at the [[University of Texas]], she joined the University of Washington in 2002.<ref name="closeup"/> In 2019, she became the chair of the biostatistics department.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hodson |first1=Jeff |title=Lurdes Inoue appointed chair of Biostatistics |url=https://sph.washington.edu/news-events/news/lurdes-inoue-appointed-chair-biostatistics |website=University of Washington School of Public Health |accessdate=19 March 2020}}</ref>

==Book==
With [[Giovanni Parmigiani]], she is the author of the book ''Decision Theory: Principles and Approaches'' (Wiley, 2009).<ref>{{citation
 | last = Bornkamp | first = Björn
 | date = February 2010
 | doi = 10.1007/s00362-010-0318-5
 | issue = 4
 | journal = Statistical Papers
 | pages = 985–986
 | title = G. Parmigiani and L. Inoue: Decision theory–principles and approaches
 | volume = 52| s2cid = 118399995
 }}.</ref> This book won the DeGroot Prize of the [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]] for 2009.<ref>[https://bayesian.org/awards/DeGrootPrize.html DeGroot Prize], [[International Society for Bayesian Analysis]], retrieved 2016-07-13.</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2014, Inoue was elected as a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Statistical Association]] "for substantial and fundamental contributions to Bayesian decision theory and innovation in the statistical modeling of disease progression with applications to cancer research; for outstanding mentoring of junior researchers; and for exemplary service to the profession."<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.amstat.org/newsroom/pressreleases/2014_ASAFellows.pdf|title=ASA Honors 63 New Fellows|publisher=[[American Statistical Association]]|date=June 11, 2014|accessdate=2016-07-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304054602/http://www.amstat.org/newsroom/pressreleases/2014_ASAFellows.pdf|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}.</ref>
